comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh current 2026–2027 Mathematics and Computer Science after-revision PER, Articles 3.3–3.5 and Appendix 2 Applied Mathematics table p.78, establishes the ordinary English full-time single-degree curriculum. Twenty-eight credited positions total 60 + 60 + 60 = 180: core 125 including ordinary 2MBB10 Bachelor Final Project exactly 10, ITEC 10 and genuine open electives 45 (15 in year two, 30 in year three). Current Calculus for Applied Mathematics 2MCALCAM replaces 2WCB0 for September-2026 entrants under Appendix 3 p.90; no extra calculus is added. No formal specialization is required; select the broad ordinary pathway independently of UCR fit. Article 3.4 permits an alternative interdisciplinary Innovation Space final project of 15 EC by derogation; this is an optional alternative, not an extra requirement or a generic 10/15/20 range. The ordinary 10-credit final project spans two quarter positions and counts once. SCOP/e 2PRV21/2PRV22 and PPD are embedded; core CBL subparts add no credits. MyFuture requires value seven with no EC; at least five Studium Generale activities are part of ITEC requirements. Open electives require examination-board approval, no substantive overlap and at least 30 EC at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3. BEP entry requires at least 120 credits including all compulsory first-year units; the 95-BCS-credit rule belongs to Computer Science, not Applied Mathematics. Multidisciplinary CBL requires completion of offered PPD-containing components. Detailed course assessment conditions and future timetabling remain applicable catalogue conditions. core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and system models
Statistics, data analysis, stochastic modelling and empirical prediction
Programming, algorithms, optimisation and scientific computation
adjacent: Mathematical models of physical, industrial and sustainable systems

applies regression, factor analysis, ANOVA and other multivariate models to real-world research data
develops logic, discrete structures and patterns for mathematical reasoning and algorithm construction
implements reinforcement-learning algorithms and neural-network agents for stochastic adaptive decisions

develops algorithm and data-structure design with performance analysis

develops data preparation, visualisation and manipulation for empirical mathematical analysis
implements regression, resampling, shrinkage and tree-based statistical learning methods
applies numerical image representations, feature detection and tracking to technological data
develops neural-network and deep-learning models for prediction and computer vision
supplies programming, testing and debugging for implementing mathematical algorithms and models

implements numerical equation solving, interpolation, integration and differential equations with error and stability analysis

uses technical and economic analysis to assess energy demand and solar, wind and bioenergy system designs

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, algorithms & stochastic data models
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and linear systems alongside programming, algorithms, optimisation, statistical learning, image analysis and robotics. Economic and human-data models provide concrete empirical applications. Proof-intensive analysis and algebra remain important differences from the full Applied Mathematics curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: Nineteen mathematical/computational courses plus four concrete statistical and decision-model applications support the label without claiming the external programme’s proof-intensive mathematical depth.
progression: All current offerings and formal earlier prerequisites checked. Programming precedes image processing and statistical learning; machine learning precedes deep learning, linear algebra precedes robotics, and first empirical methods precede later human-data statistics where included. These preferences do not create new formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, computational systems & sustainable technology
alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical and computational system modelling while applying it to climate, renewable-energy and sustainability problems through scientific foundations, technical/economic energy assessment and autonomous technology.
alternatives.labelReason: Four sustainability/energy courses replace four statistics/economics applications and create a distinct physical-system and technology application strand.
progression: All current offerings and formal earlier prerequisites checked. Programming precedes image processing and statistical learning; machine learning precedes deep learning, linear algebra precedes robotics, and first empirical methods precede later human-data statistics where included. These preferences do not create new formal prerequisites.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Introductory economics, research methods, advanced human-data statistics and econometrics are replaced by two sustainability-science foundations, climate change and renewable-system design. These changes implement the evidenced physical/industrial-system application direction.

blocks: Both develop formal logic and mathematical language; UCR emphasises discrete structures and algorithm construction.
Both establish calculus for applied models; UCR also includes differential equations and dynamic modelling, with applications beyond mathematics.
Both directly study linear algebra; the external second linear-algebra component remains separate additional depth.
Both directly develop numerical methods and error/stability reasoning.
Both address differential equations; UCR combines them with multivariable and complex calculus rather than the same ODE theory sequence.

Fourier and Laplace transforms, convolution and frequency-domain methods directly overlap part of the transform curriculum. UCR focuses on signals and linear systems rather than the full generating-function and transform-theorem treatment.
Both establish probability and modelling; UCR integrates mathematical statistics and simulation.
Both use regression models for empirical prediction; econometrics specialises them to economic relationships.
Both provide statistical inference; UCR applies advanced models to human data rather than the same theoretical statistics syllabus.

Partial correspondence through temporal probabilistic and Markov decision models. The TU/e course additionally develops Poisson, continuous-time and birth-and-death processes and stationary distributions.

Partial correspondence through linear programming, discrete optimisation and computational modelling within a broader optimisation course; TU/e also develops duality, simplex theory, integer and network optimisation.
Partial relationship through graph algorithms and algorithm analysis. UCR also studies broader data structures; TU/e develops a wider graph-theory and proof sequence.
Both use programming to construct mathematical models; UCR provides broader computer-science foundations.

notes.text: The UCR options develop applied mathematical and computational methods, including some formal proofs, linear programming, graph algorithms and stochastic models. They do not reproduce TU/e’s full proof-intensive analysis, algebra, measure theory and specialist mathematics sequence or its compulsory final project.

audience.programmeDescription: Applied Mathematics develops mathematical models for practical problems, solves them with theoretical and computational methods, and interprets the results for the original problem. The curriculum combines analysis, algebra, probability, statistics, optimisation and scientific computing.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR options develop related mathematical and computational methods. The first adds empirical models of economic and human data; the second adds physical-science, climate and energy applications. Several correspondences are partial, and TU/e’s full specialist mathematical depth and compulsory project remain important differences.

curriculum.limitation: Elective selections require approval and must meet the programme’s level and non-overlap rules.

componentNotes.2MBB10: Required 10 EC ordinary final project, counted once across its two quarter positions. Entry requires at least 120 EC, including all compulsory first-year study. The interdisciplinary Innovation Space project is an alternative and is not added to this curriculum.
componentNotes.4CBLW00: Requires completion of previously offered study embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organisation skills.
componentNotes.cp-000274-y2-open: 15 EC of approved elective study in year 2 and 30 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC must be intermediate or advanced, including 15 EC advanced. Content must not overlap. Submit the complete 180 EC plan for approval after earning at least 90 EC; changes also need approval.
componentNotes.0LVX20: Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. At least five Studium Generale activities are required within ITEC. Personal and professional development, SCOP/e and other challenges are embedded. MyFuture activities with a combined value of seven add no credits.
